newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ukraine believes Chernobyl problems will be solved.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine believes Chernobyl problems will be solved.

text.p: Ukrainian deputy prime minister Victor Pynzenyk said on Friday he believed problems blocking the closure of a reactor at the stricken Chernobyl nuclear plant in the Ukraine would be resolved.
"Ukraine has a greater stake than anyone else in finding a solution and the specialists are working on it," he told reporters.
He was speaking at a World Bank news conference at which international donors agreed to help fill the country's 1.8 billion external financing gap for 1997.

Ukraine, which has promised to close the station by the year 2000 in exchange for $3 billion in grants and funding from the Group of Seven industrialised nations, gave assurances to G7 leaders in April that it would close the reactor in October.
But it said earlier this month that it might be too dangerous to carry out the promise because of technical problems that might make the station prone to an accident.
"In Ukraine, the political decision (to shut Chernobyl) has been made," said Roman Shpek, head of the Ukrainian National Agency of Reconstruction and Development.
"The engineering and technical work needs to take place," he told the news conference.
He said a list of technical and engineering procedures needed to be drawn up to guarantee the security of the shutdown process. There was also a need "to ensure financial sources", he said.
Ukraine has repeatedly complained about the West's failure to deliver money for shutting the plant but recently said progress had been made.
